item.title: Anatomy of an Autonomous Attack: 5 Alarming A.I. Capabilities
item.description: When OpenAI’s agents went rogue in July, they demonstrated ingenuity and drive beyond what many experts imagined — a dangerous harbinger of what such bots could do in the future.
item.dc:creator: Dylan Freedman
item.media:credit: The New York Times; source photos by Aaron Wojack and Ulysses Ortega for The New York Times

item.title: Wildfires Are Turning Forests in the American West Into Shrubland
item.description: Towering woodlands in the West are being permanently replaced by tracts of spiky shrubs. Conditions “just aren’t normal anymore,” one researcher said.
item.dc:creator: Eric Niiler and Nic Coury

item.title: Mapping America’s Largest ‘Dead Zone’
item.description: In a decades-long crisis, marine life has suffered as oxygen periodically dwindles in waters along the Gulf Coast.

item.title: Trump Announces a New Policy for a ‘Golden Age of Space Transportation’
item.description: The policy aims to greatly increase the number of spacecraft launches and re-entries.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Chang
item.media:description: The Trump administration wants to increase to 1,000 the number of rocket launches and spacecraft re-entries from space per year.

item.title: England’s Ancient Trees Are Dying in the Heat
item.description: Extreme temperatures and drought are adding to the stress on oak trees that have lived for hundreds of years and play a key role in the national imagination.
item.dc:creator: Claire Moses
item.media:credit: Royal Society for the Protection of Birds, via Associated Press
item.media:description: The Major Oak at Sherwood Forest Nature Reserve in Nottinghamshire, England, in May.

item.title: This Skeleton is the First Confirmed Death by Trebuchet
item.description: Researchers believe a young man buried inside a Scottish castle was a victim of the long-feared siege weapon, more powerful than a typical catapult.
item.dc:creator: K. R. Callaway

item.title: NASA’s Attempt to Save the Swift Telescope Has Failed
item.description: NASA’s Swift Observatory, which studies some of the most powerful explosions in the universe, will soon burn up in the atmosphere.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Chang

item.title: Humans Love Having Pets. Seems Like Some Other Primates Do, Too.
item.description: We aren’t the only animals that like to take care of other species. A new study finds that the roots of keeping a pet may stretch deep into our primate past.
item.dc:creator: Taylor Mitchell Brown

item.title: Nevada Sues Trump Administration Over Colorado River Cuts
item.description: The state seeks to block plans for significant water use restrictions over the next decade.
item.dc:creator: Scott Dance
item.media:credit: L.E. Baskow/Las Vegas Review-Journal, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Nevada argued in a lawsuit that federal officials did not impose mandatory water restrictions on states in the Colorado River’s upper basin.

item.title: The Ruthless Efficiency of Ultrapotent Street Drugs
item.description: Five decades after the “war on drugs” sought to make substance abuse unaffordable, illicit drugs are cheaper and more powerful than ever. A visit to Baltimore shows why.
item.dc:creator: Matt Richtel
item.media:credit: KT Kanazawich for The New York Times
item.media:description: Last summer, the city of Baltimore experienced several mass overdose crises, the result of fentanyl being mixed with powerful synthetic chemicals.

item.title: Trump Shuns E.V.s and Wind Power, But He’s Pouring Billions Into Batteries
item.description: The president may disdain clean energy tech, but energy storage is also crucial for A.I. and defense — and China’s dominance in the sector has officials worried.
item.dc:creator: Brad Plumer
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Brandon Thibodeaux for The New York Times
item.media:description: While the Trump administration has rolled back efforts to expand clean energy, officials have come to see batteries as essential for many of their priorities.

item.title: Why Getting High Has Only Gotten Cheaper
item.description: The “war on drugs” sought to reduce substance abuse by driving up prices and lowering demand. Today, street drugs are less expensive and more dangerous than ever.
item.dc:creator: Matt Richtel and Irena Hwang

item.title: U.S. Cuts Colorado River Water for Arizona, California and Nevada
item.description: Arizona’s share of the river will shrink by a third, likely increasing reliance on groundwater and raising pressure on agriculture.
item.dc:creator: Scott Dance
item.media:description: The Colorado River at Horseshoe Bend near Page, Ariz., last month.

item.title: Climate: Trump vs. California
item.description: At least a half-dozen federal agencies have moved to undermine the state’s environmental efforts.
item.dc:creator: Maxine Joselow
item.media:description: President Trump signed a measure in June 2025 to block a California rule that would have barred the sale of new gas-powered cars by 2035.

item.title: Climate: Saving Old Trees Might Save Lives
item.description: We know that trees are good for cities. A new study finds that mature trees are especially good.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Nazaryan
item.media:description: Researchers working with satellite images of Chicago matched changes in tree canopy in different neighborhoods over the years with mortality rates in those areas.

item.title: Moderna’s Shift to Cancer Company Lifts Stock Up 177%
item.description: The company’s fortunes cratered as demand for Covid-19 vaccines plummeted. But it was busy working on something else.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Robbins
item.media:description: A lab at Moderna’s headquarters in Cambridge, Mass., in 2024.

item.title: How Trump Is Trying to Crush California’s Climate Policies
item.description: At least a half-dozen federal agencies have taken action against the state that has led the nation in environmental protections.

item.media:credit: Ariana Drehsler for The New York Times
item.media:description: An oil platform seen from Sands Beach next to Coal Oil Point Natural Reserve in Santa Barbara, Calif.

item.title: Chinese Start-Up Lands Reusable Rocket for the First Time
item.description: The milestone by the private company, LandSpace, could put China closer to challenging SpaceX’s rule in lower-cost spaceflight.

item.title: Former Fauci Adviser Pleads Guilty to Trying to Conceal Covid-Related Records
item.description: Dr. David Morens, a former N.I.H. official, admitted to attempts to conceal emails that discussed the origins of the pandemic.

item.media:description: David Morens, a former National Institutes of Health official, after his arraignment in the U.S. District Court in Greenbelt, Md., in May.

item.title: Moderna, Merck Say mRNA Vaccine Prevents Melanoma From Returning
item.description: Moderna and Merck say the experimental vaccine prevented the return and spread of the cancer in high-risk melanoma patients.
item.dc:creator: Carolyn Y. Johnson
item.media:description: Cancer vaccine research in the lab at the Moderna Inc. headquarters in Cambridge, Mass.

item.title: Trump Nominates Heidi Overton, a Top Domestic Policy Aide, for F.D.A. Commissioner
item.description: Dr. Overton is a fierce opponent of abortion rights and a supporter of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s Make America Healthy Again agenda.
item.dc:creator: Christina Jewett
item.media:credit: Eric Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dr. Heidi Overton, if confirmed by the Senate, would succeed Dr. Marty Makary, who resigned as commissioner in May.

item.title: Trump Administration Moves to Allow Logging in Pristine National Forests
item.description: The move to repeal the ‘roadless rule’ would pave the way for road construction and logging in nearly 45 million acres of untouched back country.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Friedman and Maxine Joselow
item.media:description: A bear in the Tongass National Forest of southeast Alaska. Roadless areas make up about 30 percent of all national forest land and are home to more than half of imperiled wildlife, including grizzly bears, wolves, elk, salmon and wolverines.

item.title: Rafting Through the Grand Canyon on a Depleting Colorado River
item.description: As water levels on the Colorado River fall to historic lows, a rafting trip through the canyon feels even more precious.
item.dc:creator: Heather Hansman
item.media:description: For rafters beginning their journey on the Colorado River through the Grand Canyon, Navajo Bridge is the last modern structure they see for the trip’s duration.

item.title: How NASA Engineers Are Keeping the Voyagers Alive
item.description: A reworking of the spacecraft’s power systems could extend the nearly 50-year-old Voyagers’ exploration of interstellar space into the early 2030s.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Chang
item.media:credit: Ariana Drehsler for The New York Times
